payload.description_html: A Lophiodes miacanthus or monkfish, on display at the Smithsonian Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. These are a species of fish that belong to the anglerfish family. Lophiodes miacanthus was first discovered in 1905. It is a benthic fish, which means it lives right on the sandy bottom of the continental shelf (rather than in deep oceanic water). This sub-species lives in the Pacific Ocean near Hawaii and along the eastern coast of Asia in warm waters about 350 to 3000 feet deep. These fish grow to be about 6 inches long. They have huge mouths, which are better for nabbing prey. They have two hind fins, which they use to propel themselves along the sandy bottom.
